messages:
maria: Hey support, customer on prod is seeing the Python generator hang after partial tokens when we rotate the API key. Repro environment: python3.10, redwood-sdk 0.5.1, Ubuntu 20.04.

maria: Minimal repro snippet:
```
from redwood import StreamClient
client = StreamClient(api_key='rotating-key')
for chunk in client.stream('chat.completions', model='open-llama'):
    print(chunk)
```

oliver: tagging @eng-runtime — can you check server logs? any 499/connection reset?

maria: server logs show intermittent 'partial_event' frames and then no final 'data: [DONE]' event. Connection remains open and heartbeats (':\n') are sent every 15s. Client generator never yields the final aggregate token and user sees the UI spinner.

sam: sounds like a framing mismatch. 0.6.0 changed the SSE parser to accept optional 'event:' headers before 'data:' and treat a blank line as emit. 0.5.1 expects a pure data-first stream and will wait if it sees unknown headers.

maria: confirmed: upgrading to redwood==0.6.0 on a repro box resolves it immediately. Downgrading to 0.5.1 reproduces the hang.

jess: short-term workaround: set REDWOOD_STREAM_COMPAT=loose to use tolerant parsing. Long-term: we'll backport a fix to the 0.5.x branch to handle 'event:' headers and split partial tokens.

oliver: created support ticket #12345 and scheduled a maintenance window for the customer's instance. I also pushed a quick hotfix to the internal edge that injects an extra newline on 'event:' header sequences.

sam: can someone write a minimal unit test covering: header+data, header-only heartbeat, and mid-chunk split tokens? I can take the header+heartbeat test.

jess: I'll do the split-token test. Also adding an integration test in CI with chunked transfer and random chunk boundaries.

maria: customer accepted upgrade plan, will roll tomorrow morning PST. Thanks all :thumbsup:

support-bot: ticket #12345 updated: state -> scheduled by oliver (ETA 2026-03-18)
